product_overview: A security and access control module for an ERP-style application, providing authentication, self-service account recovery, and administrative management of users, roles, permissions, pages, and data access scope. It also supports notification-related account recovery flows and a mock local notifications workspace.
core_goals: Sign in to the application and reach the dashboard
Create and activate a new user account
Manage users, roles, permissions, and page registry entries
Assign page permissions and copy them between roles
Configure user profiles and role-based branch data scope
View and manage notification inbox, templates, and channels in the local UI

features.name: User Authentication and Self-Service
features.description: Lets a visitor sign in, create an account, activate it, request a password reset, and set a new password from the login screen.
user_flows: Navigate to /(login) -> Fill in username -> Fill in password -> Submit login form -> See dashboard
Navigate to /(login) -> Fill in username -> Fill in password -> Submit login form with incorrect credentials -> See an error message and remain on the login screen
Navigate to /(login) -> Switch to the Signup tab -> Fill in username, email, and password -> Submit the form -> See confirmation that the account needs activation
Navigate to /(login) -> Switch to the Activate account tab -> Enter activation code -> Submit the form -> See success confirmation and regain ability to log in
Navigate to /(login) -> Switch to the Forgot password tab -> Enter account email -> Submit the form -> See confirmation message
Navigate to /(login) -> Switch to the Reset password tab -> Enter reset token and new password -> Submit the form -> See confirmation that the password was updated

features.name: Dashboard Navigation
features.description: Provides the post-login landing page and entry points into the main security administration areas.
user_flows: Navigate to /(dashboard) after successful login -> See the dashboard landing screen -> Choose a navigation card or link -> Open the selected module screen

features.name: Security Users Management
features.description: Allows an administrator to search, create, edit, delete, and profile-manage user accounts, including role assignment and data scope access.
user_flows: Navigate to /(sec-users) -> Enter a search term -> Apply status or role filters -> See the filtered user list
Navigate to /(sec-users) -> Start creating a new user -> Fill in the required user details -> Submit the form -> See the new user appear in the list
Navigate to /(sec-users) -> Open a user for editing -> Change the user details -> Update the assigned roles -> Save changes -> See the updated user details persist
Navigate to /(sec-users) -> Open a user's profile drawer -> Edit extended profile fields -> Save changes -> Reopen the drawer -> See the saved profile values
Navigate to /(sec-users) -> Open the data scope drawer for a user or role -> Change branch-level access settings -> Save changes
Navigate to /(sec-users) -> Choose to delete a user -> Confirm the deletion -> See the user removed from the list
Navigate to /(sec-users) -> Choose to delete a user with linked data -> Confirm the deletion -> See a conflict message and remain on the list

features.name: Security Roles and RBAC Management
features.description: Lets an administrator create and maintain roles, activate or deactivate them, manage page permissions, and copy permissions from another role.
user_flows: Navigate to /(sec-roles) -> Enter a role search term -> Apply filters -> See filtered role results
Navigate to /(sec-roles) -> Start creating a new role -> Fill in the required role fields -> Submit the form -> See the new role appear in the list
Navigate to /(sec-roles) -> Open a role for editing -> Change the role fields -> Save changes -> See the updated role values persist
Navigate to /(sec-roles) -> Deactivate an active role -> Confirm the action -> See the role status change to inactive
Navigate to /(sec-roles) -> Activate an inactive role -> Confirm the action -> See the role status change to active
Navigate to /(sec-roles) -> Open the permission matrix drawer -> Toggle page permission values -> Save changes -> Reopen the drawer -> See the updates persist
Navigate to /(sec-roles) -> Open the permission matrix drawer -> Remove a page's permission row -> Save changes -> Reopen the drawer -> See the removed row stay removed

Navigate to /(sec-roles) -> Open the permission matrix drawer -> Choose to copy permissions from another role -> Pick a source role -> Confirm the copy -> See the target role reflect the source role's permissions

features.name: Security Permissions Registry
features.description: Allows an administrator to search, create, and edit raw permission records directly.
user_flows: Navigate to /(sec-permissions) -> Enter a permission search term -> Apply a module filter -> See the filtered permission list
Navigate to /(sec-permissions) -> Start creating a new permission -> Fill in code, module, and description -> Submit the form -> See the new permission appear in the list
Navigate to /(sec-permissions) -> Open a permission for editing -> Change the name or description -> Save changes -> See the updated permission values persist

features.name: Security Page Registry
features.description: Allows an administrator to search, create, edit, deactivate, and reactivate page registry entries that drive permissions and navigation.
user_flows: Navigate to /(sec-pages) -> Enter a page search term -> Apply filters -> See the filtered page list
Navigate to /(sec-pages) -> Start creating a new page -> Fill in the required page fields -> Submit the form -> See the new page appear and its permissions generated
Navigate to /(sec-pages) -> Open a page for editing -> Change the page details -> Save changes -> See the updated values persist
Navigate to /(sec-pages) -> Deactivate an active page -> Confirm the action -> See the page status change to inactive
Navigate to /(sec-pages) -> Reactivate an inactive page -> Confirm the action -> See the page status change to active

features.name: User Profile and Branch Data Scope
features.description: Lets an administrator maintain a user's extended profile and set the user's or role's branch-level access scope.
user_flows: Navigate to /(sec-users) -> Open a user's profile drawer -> Update the user's name, employee link, or preferred language -> Save changes -> Reopen the drawer -> See the saved profile values
Navigate to /(sec-users) -> Open a user's data scope drawer -> Choose a branch-level access setting -> Save changes -> See the updated access scope persist
Navigate to /(sec-users) -> Open the user profile entry flow -> Select a branch -> Save the profile -> See the profile linked to the chosen branch
Navigate to /(sec-roles) -> Open the role data scope panel -> Assign a branch and access level -> Save changes -> See the role scope entry persist

features.name: Notifications Workspace
features.description: Provides a local-state notifications inbox, template manager, and channel manager within the frontend.
user_flows: Navigate to /(notif-inbox) -> Review the notification inbox -> Open a notification item -> See its details
Navigate to /(notif-templates) -> Create a new notification template -> Fill in the template details -> Save changes -> See the template appear in the list
Navigate to /(notif-templates) -> Open an existing template -> Edit its content -> Save changes -> See the updated template persist in the UI
Navigate to /(notif-channels) -> Create a new notification channel -> Fill in the channel details -> Save changes -> See the channel appear in the list
Navigate to /(notif-channels) -> Open a channel for editing -> Update its settings -> Save changes -> See the updated channel persist in the UI

tech_stack: Custom design-system UI kit (Button, Table, FormControls, Drawer, Toast, Pagination)

routes.description: Single-page app, no URL router — App.tsx gates the whole UI on isAuthenticated and switches screens via an in-memory navigation store (useNavigationStore.currentScreen), not real URLs. Unauthenticated users always see Login; authenticated users see AppShell with the screen matching currentScreen.
Login screen, containing tabs for Login, Signup, Activate account, Forgot password, and Reset password (all client-side tabs on one screen, not separate URLs).
Landing screen after login; navigation entry point to other modules.
Security > Users list/search/create/edit/delete, with drawers for profile and role assignment.
Security > Roles list/search/create/edit/deactivate/activate, permission-matrix drawer, copy-permissions-from-role, data-scope drawer.
Notifications inbox — mock/local-state only, not backend-connected.
Notification templates — mock/local-state only, not backend-connected.
Notification channels — mock/local-state only, not backend-connected.

known_limitations.issue: (FIXED 2026-08-29, needs re-verification this run) Role/Page Registry Create and Save controls, and Permission Matrix checkboxes, were hidden/disabled for every user
known_limitations.impact: Root cause was a permission-literal mismatch — these hooks checked bare literals like 'ROLE_CREATE' instead of the real backend authority 'PERM_ROLE_CREATE', so can() always returned false. Fixed by adding the missing PERM_ prefix everywhere; manually verified in-browser (Add New / Save Changes now render, Permission Matrix checkboxes now toggle and persist via Sync All). This TestSprite run should confirm TC013/TC016/TC017/TC020/TC023/TC024-equivalent flows now pass.

known_limitations.issue: Permissions search + module filter combo returns zero results
known_limitations.impact: Searching with both a text query and a module filter applied returns no results even for permissions known to exist, while the equivalent Page Registry search works correctly — likely a module-code mismatch specific to the permissions search request. Confirmed in the 2026-08-28 TestSprite run; not touched by the 2026-08-29 permission-literal fix, status unconfirmed.

known_limitations.issue: Deleting a user with existing linked data (roles, profile) returns a conflict
known_limitations.impact: Likely expected backend referential-integrity/session protection (error code ERR-SEC-049-DELETE, "Cannot delete a user with active sessions"), not a frontend bug. Confirmed in the 2026-08-29 TestSprite run against a user with linked data.

known_limitations.issue: Notifications module is UI-only, not connected to backend API
known_limitations.impact: Inbox/templates/channels are mock/local-state only; changes are not persisted server-side.
